# KCH ChatGPT Projection

Prefer native integration in this order: host instructions, precise skills, lifecycle hooks, local
tools and personal plugin; use MCP only for a documented external capability gap.

## Projection matrix

1. Treat plugin skills as the portable behavioral layer on ChatGPT surfaces that support them.
2. Treat Project instructions as project-scoped governance inherited by chats inside that project.
3. Treat Codex `AGENTS.md`, hooks and bundled Python runtimes as local Codex-host capabilities.
4. Do not claim web or mobile can execute a local hook, filesystem runtime or background daemon.
5. Do not claim Codex IDE-extension support merely because Codex desktop or CLI supports a plugin.
6. Keep unrelated project instructions sovereign; distribute KCH universally through the supported
   plugin layer instead of overwriting every project indiscriminately.

## Validation

For each surface, record separately: discoverable, installable, enabled, skill visible, instruction
loaded, hook observed, runtime executable and action authorized. Open a new session or reload when
host activation requires it. A copied file or successful package install is not activation evidence.

Report the maximum real deployment and every gap. When a surface cannot host local execution,
provide the behavior/governance layer there and route external capability through a governed
connector only if needed.
